text:
Dallas is 15-8-2 with 32 points and a 75% playoff chance by our simulations, and the man most responsible is in the crease. Jake Oettinger is .949 over his last five starts, 8.9 goals better than expected, with his fifth shutout of the season coming against Pittsburgh. As a team the Stars have allowed almost twelve fewer goals than their chances against would predict. At the other end they've scored about nine fewer than theirs, and the overall picture is a coin-flip team on chances (50.7% of the expected goals) riding a goalie.

That shortage of finishing is the thing to fix, and it's strange given the names. Jason Robertson, playing through another contract year after the reported $125 million Seattle offer he wouldn't comment on, scored twice Friday in a 5-3 loss in St. Louis, a game Dallas deserved to win 60% of the time on chances. The Stars take 4.0 penalties a game, too many for a team that relies on a thin margin.

Jamie Benn's 1,000th point earlier this month was the warm story of the season. Nils Lundkvist and Thomas Harley are the best pair, 54% of the expected goals and 14-11 in goals. Lines have been shuffled all season, with no forward trio past 84 minutes together. Watch whether the scoring catches up before Oettinger cools.
